title: How does a line learn?
hook: No formula, no maths homework: just a line that is told when it is wrong.

knows: that a straight line can separate two groups of points
doesNotKnow: how a separating line can be learned by small corrections
that the perceptron changes only when it gets a point wrong

misconception: A line is fitted by one calculation; it cannot improve in small steps.
objective: The learner can explain that a perceptron checks points one at a time, changes its line only on a mistake, and each nudge moves the line toward putting the missed point on the right side.

claims.text: Starting from zero weights and sweeping (1,1)+, (−1,0)−, (2,−1)+, (−1,−2)−, (0,2)+ in order, the perceptron nudges at (1,1) (weights 1,1, offset 1) and at (−1,0) (weights 2,1, offset 0); the second sweep has no mistakes: 2 nudges in all.
claims.source: checkOne() / untilClean() in Demo.tsx with the rule w ← w + label·(x, y, 1) when label·score ≤ 0. Node: nudge at (1,1) → [1,1,1]; nudge at (−1,0) → [2,1,0]; sweep 1 mistakes 2, sweep 2 mistakes 0.

claims.text: In this toy a point is right when it sits on its own side of the line (+ in the shaded side, − outside); a zero score counts as wrong, so with no line every point counts as wrong and the very first point is nudged.
claims.source: Toy convention stated on the locked caption in Demo.tsx (v2) and in checkOne(): wrong if label·score ≤ 0; shaded side is w·x + b ≥ 0. Brief 33 in company/domains/briefs/ai.md. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): checkOne(): wrong if l*score <= 0; shaded polygon is w.x + b >= 0; with w = 0 every score is 0, so (1,1) is nudged first (own trace). Locked caption says the same.

claims.text: A perceptron changes its weights only when it misclassifies a point, by adding or subtracting that point.
claims.source: Rosenblatt 1958, 'The perceptron: a probabilistic model for information storage and organization in the brain', Psychological Review 65(6); the error-correction rule in modern form: Bishop 2006, Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning, §4.1.7.

claims.text: Each nudge moves the line toward putting the missed point on its own side (on stage, a red ring turns green): the missed point's score rises by |point|² + 1 (for a + point) or falls by as much (for a − point); points already right change nothing.
claims.source: After w ← w + l·(x, y, 1), the point's score changes by l·(x² + y² + 1). Bishop 2006 §4.1.7 (the update reduces that point's error). On stage: (1,1) and (−1,0) both turn from red to green after their nudges (trace in Demo.tsx header). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): Own trace: (1,1)+ score 0 -> 3 (rise 1+1+1 = 3); (-1,0)- score 0 -> -2 (fall 1+0+1 = 2); both rings go red -> green; a point already right triggers no update. Bishop 2006 section 4.1.7 not opened; matches my knowledge.

claims.text: The 'Rest of sweep' caption lists every nudge made in that sweep; on the recommended path it reads '(−1,0) −: score 0 → wrong, nudge. Then 3 points right, no change.', and each nudged point is labelled 'nudge 1', 'nudge 2' on the stage.
claims.source: restOfSweep() in Demo.tsx v2: after nudge 1 w = (1,1,1); (−1,0) scores −1 + 0 + 1 = 0 → nudge to (2,1,0); (2,−1) scores 3, (−1,−2) scores −4, (0,2) scores 2: all right. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 21): Own copy of restOfSweep(): after one 'Check next point', caption reads '(-1,0) −: score 0 → wrong, nudge. Then 3 points right, no change.'; labels nudge 1 (1,1), nudge 2 (-1,0). The stage prints the coordinate with an ASCII hyphen '(-1,0)' where the claim has '(−1,0)': typographic only.

recall.question: A perceptron's line already puts a point on the correct side. What does that point do to the line on the next sweep?
options: Nothing: only mistakes change the line
Pulls the line a little closer to it
Pushes the line a little further away
recall.why: The perceptron updates only when it gets a point wrong (or scores it exactly 0). Correct points leave the weights alone.
